issues.legal_issue: A cess assessed using a measure of property profits other than profits determined under the business-income rules is not barred from deduction merely because its assessment is related to profits.
material_facts: The assessee carried on a coal-mining business and, as lessee of mines, incurred liability for road, public works and education cesses.

The cesses were assessed by reference to annual net profits calculated under the cess legislation, generally using an average of prior years’ profits, with a property-value estimate available if those profits could not be ascertained.
The cesses were not levied on the profits or gains of the business, and the profits used to assess them were not calculated under the business-income rules.
The assessee claimed the cesses as deductions in computing its business profits, and the tax authorities disallowed the claims.
issues.conclusion: The cesses were not excluded from deduction by section 10(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, and were deductible under section 10(2)(ix) or section 10(2)(xv), as applicable.
issues.legal_principle: In context, the reference in section 10(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1922, to profits and gains of a business means profits determined under section 10, not profits calculated by another method. Section 10(4) excludes a cess, rate or tax whose assessment follows determination of business profits under that section, including one levied on those profits or assessed proportionately or otherwise on their basis. The provisions governing the cesses here, including sections 72 to 76 of the Bengal Cess Act, 1880, and the corresponding scheme under the Bengal (Rural) Primary Education Act, 1930, used a different measure. The Court applied Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal v. Gurupada Datta, followed Simbholi Sugar Mill Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P. and V.P. and Commissioner of Income-tax, Delhi and Rajasthan v. Banarsi Dass & Sons, and disapproved Commissioner of Income-tax, West Bengal v. West Bengal Mining Co.

rule.if: business_tax_deduction_dispute and cess_imposed_on_business_property and cess_assessed_using_non_tax_profit_measure and expense_otherwise_business_deductible

predicates.business_tax_deduction_dispute: A taxpayer claimed a business-related cess as a deduction in computing business income, and the tax authority disputed that deduction.
predicates.cess_imposed_on_business_property: The cess liability arose because the taxpayer held or used property in connection with its business.
predicates.cess_assessed_using_non_tax_profit_measu: The cess was assessed using a measure of property profits or value that was not the measure used to determine taxable business profits.
predicates.expense_otherwise_business_deductible: Apart from the statutory exclusion at issue, the claimed cess qualified as a business deduction.

issues.definition: When a business-deduction dispute concerns a property-related cess assessed using a non-tax profit measure and otherwise qualifying as a business deduction, the cess is not barred from that deduction.
